text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Separatist Northern League leader Umberto Bossi came under attack from all sides for accusing Pope John Paul of meddling in domestic politics. Bossi's comments drew harsh condemnation from the Vatican paper L'Osservatore Romano and appeared to damage attempts at forging a political alliance between the Northern League and the main centre-right opposition bloc (all).

* Foreign Ministry warned travellers to Kenya to stay clear of the Indian Ocean port city of Mombasa, which has been hit by a wave of violence in the last week. A ministry statement also urged visitors to the Kenyan capital of Nairobi to avoid the city centre and areas close to the university (all).

* Telecommunications group Telecom Italia said it had reached a deal with Banca Commerciale Italiana to take an indirect stake in publishing firm Seat. A group led by BCI, which includes publishers De Agostini, announced last month it would pay 1.58 trillion lire for 61.7 percent of Seat ordinary shares (all).

* Top designer Giorgio Armani said he was planning a corporate shake-up for his group and he was preparing to launch the company on the stock exchange. The biggest planned change in the structure would be the incorporation into S. Andrea Srl of the Italian boutiques of Giorgio Armani and Emporio Armani. The stylistic and financial branches of the group would be independent (all).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
